meta.title: Best Muslim App for iPhone 2026: The Honest Ranking
meta.description: Looking for the best Muslim app for iPhone 2026? We ranked the top picks honestly — from the Quran on your lock screen to prayer times, reading, and hifz.

sections.title: Quick Answer
sections.content: The **best Muslim app for iPhone 2026** for most people is QuranWall, because it puts an ayah of the Quran on your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, so you see it without opening an app. For reading, prayer times or memorization, add a specialist app from the list below. QuranWall is our app, so we rank it first.

sections.text: Search for the **best Muslim app for iPhone 2026** and you get listicles that rank a dozen apps by feature count. That misses the point. The app that changes your day is not the one with the most features. It is the one you actually see. You open a reading app when you remember to. You see your lock screen all day without trying. That single fact decides this ranking.

Updated on 22 November 2026: every fact about the other four apps on this page was re-read from that app's live US App Store listing that day, and the setup steps follow how the QuranWall app works today.

sections.label: phone checks per day
sections.description: Americans say they check their phones about 186 times a day (Reviews.org, 2026 survey of about 1,000 US adults, self-reported). Your lock screen is your most-seen surface — so it is a high-leverage place to put the Quran.

sections.text: How we ranked these

One question set the order: does this app put more Quran and remembrance into your real day, or does it wait for you to come to it? Apps that meet you where you already are rank above apps that need you to show up. We did not rank on download counts, ad budgets, or how many features fit on a settings screen. Plenty of popular apps are busy without being present. Presence — showing up in your day without being summoned — is the whole game on a phone you already check constantly. Every app below is genuinely good at its job. They just answer different questions.
The five apps side by side

These five apps do different jobs, and the job is what should decide your pick. QuranWall puts an ayah on the iPhone Lock Screen and in widgets; Quran.com is for reading; Muslim Pro and Athan are prayer-time apps with a wide toolkit; Tarteel checks your recitation for hifz. The first table compares those jobs, the second the listing facts.

| App | Its main job | What it puts outside the app, per its listing | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **QuranWall** (our app) | An ayah of the Quran where you already look | The ayah you pick as your Lock Screen wallpaper, plus Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets | Daily Quran without opening an app |
| Quran - by Quran.com | Reading the mushaf | Not described in its listing | Reading, memorizing and listening to reciters |
| Muslim Pro: Quran & Athan | Prayer times and an all-round toolkit | Athan notifications and prayer widgets | Prayer times, qibla, Hijri dates and a prayer and fasting tracker |
| Tarteel: AI Quran Memorization | Memorization (hifz) | Not described in its listing | Checking your recitation from memory |
| Athan: Prayer Times, Dua Azkar | Prayer times | Azan notifications and a Home Screen prayer-times widget | Adhan alerts, plus duas, qibla and a tasbih counter |

Two things stand out. The four established apps sit between 4.7 and 4.9, so ratings barely separate them; the job does. And none of the five needs iOS 16 just to install, though QuranWall's Lock Screen wallpaper and Lock Screen widgets do. Treat both tables as a dated snapshot: listings change with every update.
1. QuranWall — best overall, and best for daily Quran

**QuranWall** is built for the iPhone Lock Screen rather than adapted to it. You pick an ayah, the app draws it as a wallpaper in one edition, Uthmani Arabic or a translation (11 editions across 10 languages), and the Shortcuts app sets it as your Lock Screen. Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets show an ayah too. You choose the background, font and colours, a preset or your own photo, and you can search all 114 surahs by surah, ayah or keyword. Each ayah has read-along recitation by Mishary Alafasy (the first play needs internet), there are no ads, and the Quran text works offline. QuranWall installs on iOS 15.0 or later; the wallpaper and Lock Screen widgets need iOS 16 or later. If you install one app from this page for daily Quran, make it this one, but other Quran widget apps exist, so compare listings before you choose. Start with the full [lock-screen setup](/blog/quran-verse-iphone-lock-screen), then pair it with a [Quran Focus mode](/blog/quran-focus-mode-iphone) for a calmer phone at set times. If you are comparing lock-screen options specifically, read our [best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone](/blog/best-islamic-lock-screen-app-iphone) ranking.
Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
2. Quran.com app — best for reading the whole Quran

When you want to sit and read, open **Quran - by Quran.com**. Its listing, from Quran Foundation, Inc, describes an ad-free mushaf app for reading the Quran, memorizing it and listening to your favourite reciters. It is a reading tool that lives behind an icon you tap, so it answers a different question than a Lock Screen app does. The smart move is both: read deeply here, and let QuranWall keep an ayah in front of you the rest of the day.
3. Muslim Pro — best for prayer times and qibla

**Muslim Pro: Quran & Athan**, from Bitsmedia Pte Ltd, is the long-running all-rounder. Its listing leads with Athan notifications calculated from your location. It then lists the full Quran with audio from multiple reciters and translations, a qibla finder, Hijri dates, a prayer and fasting tracker, and duas and dhikr with a tasbih counter. If accurate prayer alerts are your main need, it earns its place. The Quran is one part of a large toolkit there, so keep Muslim Pro for prayer timing and QuranWall for the ayah you see all day.
4. Tarteel — best for memorization (hifz)

**Tarteel: AI Quran Memorization**, from Tarteel Inc., is built for hifz. Its listing describes hiding the verses, reciting from memory and having its AI flag word-level errors, skipped words or incorrect tashkeel. It also lists voice search, which finds an ayah from a phrase you recite, and listening to qaris. The listing says listening, follow-along and voice search are free, while live mistake detection sits in its paid tier. It is a sit-down study app, and its listing does not describe a verse on the Lock Screen. Pair it with QuranWall so the ayat you are memorizing also greet you between sessions.
5. Athan by IslamicFinder — best for prayer alerts

**Athan: Prayer Times, Dua Azkar**, shown on the App Store as developed by Islamic Finder, is a prayer-times app first. Its listing describes azan notifications for the five daily prayers, a Home Screen widget with the day's prayer times, a qibla finder, an Islamic calendar, the Quran with audio, duas and athkar, and a tasbih counter. It also says that prayer-times widget is free for all users. If you want the adhan on time and the day's prayer times at a glance, it is a solid pick. Its widget shows prayer times rather than an ayah, so it sits well beside a Lock Screen Quran app. For apps built around remembrance, see our [best dhikr app for iPhone](/blog/best-dhikr-app-for-iphone) ranking.
Where this gets hard

Here is what every "just save a verse as your wallpaper" tip leaves out. A screenshot you set once stays the same until you replace it, and an image you stop noticing stops reminding you. Picking the right verse also assumes you already know where to find it. **QuranWall** answers both. It draws the ayah for the Lock Screen in the edition you chose, and you can search all 114 surahs by surah, ayah or keyword. When you want a different ayah, you pick it in the app and tap Make It Mine. The wallpaper changes only when you do that. The widget is different: it can rotate daily, every 8 hours or hourly once you turn on Auto-rotate. Less friction beats willpower here. A habit that depends on redoing a chore every morning is fragile; one built into a surface you already look at is easier to keep.

sections.content: Reading apps and prayer-time apps are not rivals to a lock-screen app — they are teammates. The reading happens in one, the seeing happens in the other. Most people are missing the seeing.

sections.text: How to set up the #1 pick

items: Download **QuranWall** from the App Store. It installs on iOS 15.0 or later; the Lock Screen wallpaper and Lock Screen widgets need iOS 16 or later.
During setup, add the QuranWall shortcut to the Shortcuts app once. The app uses it to set your Lock Screen wallpaper.
Choose your edition, Uthmani Arabic or a translation, then a background, font and colours: a preset or your own photo.
Pick an ayah, or search the 114 surahs by surah, ayah or keyword, and tap **Make It Mine**. The Shortcuts app sets it as your Lock Screen wallpaper.
Add the QuranWall widget to your Home Screen or Lock Screen. If you want the widget to show a new ayah daily, every 8 hours or hourly, turn on Auto-rotate in the app.
Optional: on iOS 16 or later you can link that Lock Screen to a **Focus** (touch and hold the Lock Screen, then tap Focus).

sections.text: Frequently asked questions
Which Muslim app puts a Quran verse on the iPhone Lock Screen?

QuranWall does: you pick an ayah, it becomes your Lock Screen wallpaper in Uthmani Arabic or a translation, and its widgets show an ayah on the Home Screen and Lock Screen. Of the other four apps here, none describes a Lock Screen verse in its US listing; Muslim Pro and Athan describe prayer-time widgets instead. Other Quran widget apps do exist, and the lock screen ranking linked above compares them.
What is a good Muslim Pro alternative?

That depends on which Muslim Pro job you want covered. For prayer times and azan alerts, Athan by IslamicFinder does the same core job. For reading and listening to the Quran, the Quran.com app is the focused, ad-free option. For an ayah on your Lock Screen, QuranWall does a job that Muslim Pro's listing does not describe. QuranWall is our app, so weigh that.
Will these apps run on an older iPhone?

Mostly. On 22 November 2026 the minimum iOS in each listing was iOS 15.0 (QuranWall and Muslim Pro), iOS 15.1 (Tarteel), iOS 15.4 (Quran.com) and iOS 15.6 (Athan), so an iPhone on an early version of iOS 15 cannot install all five. QuranWall's Lock Screen wallpaper and Lock Screen widgets need iOS 16 or later; on iOS 15 you get its Home Screen widget.
Should ratings decide which app I pick?

Not on their own. On 22 November 2026 the four established apps were rated between 4.7 and 4.9 out of 5 on the US App Store, so ratings barely separate them, and QuranWall's listing is new, with two ratings so far. Decide by the job you need done, then compare the listings.

sections.title: The short version
sections.content: For the **best Muslim app for iPhone 2026**, start with QuranWall for the Quran on your lock screen, then add a specialist: Quran.com for reading, Muslim Pro or Athan for prayer times, Tarteel for memorization. The seeing app and the reading app do different jobs — you want both.

sections.text: QuranWall is built by [Karol Billik](/about/karol-billik), an indie iOS maker, around one idea: carry the Quran onto the surface you already look at, instead of asking you to remember another app.
